title: Typography and Text Utilities
summary: Bootstrap has classes for text size, weight and alignment. Some classes make short opening text stand out.
introduction: Bootstrap has classes for text size, weight and alignment. Some classes make short opening text stand out. Choose a clear heading and paragraph first. Then try one text class at a time so you can see what each class changes.
learningObjectives: Describe the typographic defaults Reboot applies to body text and headings
Apply heading, display and lead classes to build a hierarchy
Align, transform, weight, size and colour text with utility classes
Prevent overflow with the truncation and wrapping utilities

blocks.text: With the stylesheet linked and no classes written, the body uses a **system font stack** (`system-ui`, then Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica Neue, Arial and so on), so pages render in the operating system's own typeface and load no web fonts. Body text is `1rem` (16px in most browsers) with a line height of 1.5 and the colour `#212529`. Paragraphs get `margin-bottom: 1rem`; headings get `margin-top: 0`, `margin-bottom: .5rem`, weight 500 and line height 1.2. Links are blue and underlined.

blocks.caption: Heading sizes at 1200px and wider; below that they scale down with the viewport

blocks.text: The `.h1` to `.h6` classes give any element a heading's look without changing the document outline. Use them when the visual size and the semantic level disagree: a card title that must be an `<h2>` for screen readers but should look like an `h5` gets `class="h5"`.
Headings, display headings and lead text

Ordinary headings top out at 2.5rem. For hero sections Bootstrap adds **display headings**, `.display-1` (largest, 5rem) to `.display-6` (2.5rem), which are bigger and lighter (weight 300). `.lead` makes one paragraph stand out at 1.25rem and weight 300, the usual choice for the sentence under a page title.

blocks.title: Rendered result at 1200px and wider
blocks.content:
Heading 1: 40px, weight 500
Heading 2: 32px, weight 500
Heading 3: 28px, weight 500
"A paragraph styled like an h4": 24px, weight 500, still a paragraph in the outline
Display 1: 80px, weight 300
Display 6: 40px, weight 300 (same size as Heading 1, visibly lighter)
Lead paragraph: 20px, weight 300
Normal paragraph: 16px, weight 400, 24px line height

blocks.text: On narrower screens the larger sizes shrink automatically: Bootstrap's *responsive font sizes* feature writes `h1` as `calc(1.375rem + 1.5vw)` below 1200px, so a display heading that is 80px on a desktop is a comfortable 40px or so on a phone with no extra classes.

Reboot styles the standard inline elements so you can use the semantic tag instead of a class: `<mark>` highlights, `<small>` shrinks to 87.5%, `<del>` strikes through, `<ins>` underlines, and `<abbr title="…">` gets a dotted underline with a help cursor. Block quotes need the `.blockquote` class and a `.blockquote-footer` for the source; lists can lose their bullets with `.list-unstyled` or line up horizontally with `.list-inline`.

blocks.title: Common mistake: still using text-muted
blocks.text: `text-muted` was the Bootstrap 4 way to grey out text and it still exists in 5.3, but it is deprecated and does not adapt to dark mode. Use `text-body-secondary` (and `text-body-tertiary` for even quieter text): both are defined with colour-mode-aware variables, so the same class reads correctly on light and dark backgrounds. Likewise `fw-medium` only exists from 5.3.0; on an older 5.x stylesheet it silently does nothing.

Long strings break layouts in two ways: a long sentence pushes a single-line label onto two lines, and a long URL with no spaces overflows its box. `text-truncate` solves the first by cutting the text with an ellipsis; it only works on block or inline-block elements with a constrained width, because the browser needs to know where to cut. `text-break` solves the second by allowing a break inside the word. `text-nowrap` is the opposite: it forbids wrapping entirely.

blocks.title: Ellipsis and forced breaks
blocks.code:
This sentence is far too long to fit in one hundred and eighty pixels.

https://example.com/a-very-long-path-without-any-spaces-that-would-overflow

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
First box: a single line of text ending in an ellipsis, roughly "This sentence is far…" (the exact cut depends on the font)
Second box: the URL wraps onto several lines inside the 180px box instead of spilling out of it

blocks.title: Semantic tag, visual class
blocks.text: Pick the heading level that describes the document structure, then use `.h*`, `.fs-*` or `.display-*` to get the size you want. Screen reader users navigate by heading level; the visual size is yours to choose.

questions.question: Which class produces the largest text Bootstrap offers out of the box?
questions.explanation: display-1 is 5rem on wide screens; display-6 is the smallest display heading at 2.5rem, the same size as a plain h1 or fs-1.

questions.question: The Bootstrap 5.3 replacement for the deprecated `text-muted` class is `___`.
questions.explanation: text-body-secondary uses a colour-mode-aware variable, so it stays readable when the page switches to dark mode.
